Untick it.

## The sheet comes back after analysis

The summary warns you first: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then asks you to confirm who is on each microphone, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."

When you choose **Make**, the Analyzing sheet runs. Then the sheet comes back on the same shape, **Follow**, **Zoom**, **Where Empty**, **Make a copy** and ticked microphones, this time with faces to confirm. Nothing is made until you choose **Make** there. **Stop** on the Analyzing sheet makes nothing.

## How the shot is cut

A shot is framed this way when it's a full-frame movie, its file is present, it has no cursor file, it isn't on a microphone track, and it overlaps sound on at least two ticked microphones. Frame Job doesn't count the people in it. The summary counts these shots: "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip."

Who talks when is read the way Switch by Speaker reads the microphones, with its default settings, so the two agree.

- Each change of speaker is a cut, not a move.
- Each framing holds at least 2 s, so a short reply doesn't cut away and back.
- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit. When they don't, the frame stays on the person already in it.
- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.

Every other movie clip follows its faces, and screen recordings and everything else are treated as usual. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).

## Shots that follow their faces instead

A shot that can't be framed by who is talking follows its faces instead, and the summary says why: "Clip 3 is followed, but it follows its faces, not who is talking, because …". The usual reasons are:

- It changes shot. Follow Speaker frames one wide shot, so split the clip first with **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**.
- It shows fewer faces than the microphones under it.
- Nobody talks inside it on those microphones.

## Good to know

- The faces you confirm come from the longest shot and apply to every shot by number, counting left to right. If people sit in a different order in another shot, that shot frames the wrong person.
- A shot uses only the ticked microphones that sound under it, so a microphone used elsewhere in the timeline doesn't count against it.
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) doesn't offer **Speaker**. Only Make Vertical Version and an agent do.

## With an agent

An agent makes the same version with `make_vertical_version`, naming two to four microphone clips, each standing for its track, and the faces if it wants to set them. Nobody confirms a match, so a shot whose faces don't show who is whose follows its faces, with the reason in the answer, unless the call names them. `reframe_clip` frames one clip on whoever is talking, on the canvas it's already on. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

## Related

- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: Make Vertical Version
description: Turn a landscape edit into a tall or square version for a phone, a reel or a square post, in one step over the whole timeline.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Make Vertical Version makes a tall or square version of a landscape edit, for a phone, a reel or a square post. It changes the canvas and reworks the whole timeline in one step, so you don't have to frame each clip yourself.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
  tools="make_vertical_version"
  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Make a vertical version

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. It's available when the project has a clip, no [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, no other sheet is up and nothing is recording.

2. Pick a [**Shape**](#shape).

3. Choose what to [**Follow**](#follow), and set [**Zoom**](#zoom) and [**Where Empty**](#where-empty) if you want to.

4. Leave [**Make a copy**](#make-a-copy) ticked to keep this project as it is, or untick it to change this project.

5. [Read the summary](#read-the-summary) under the controls. It says what will happen before anything does.

6. Choose **Make** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="15j-make-vertical-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Make Vertical Version sheet, with Shape on 9:16 (540 × 960), Follow on Subject, Zoom at 100 %, Where Empty on Show Whole and Make a copy ticked. The summary under them reads: Makes a 540 × 960 version. Keeps 4 clips as placed."
/>

Each clip is treated by what it is: full-frame movies follow their subject, screen recordings follow the pointer, camera layouts are laid out again, and so on. [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) goes through it clip by clip.

## The controls

### Shape

Each row shows the size it makes, such as **9:16 (1080 × 1920)**. The new canvas keeps the old short side, rounded down to an even number, and the height follows from the shape.

| Shape | From 1920 × 1080 |
| --- | --- |
| **9:16** | 1080 × 1920 |
| **4:5** | 1080 × 1350 |
| **1:1** | 1080 × 1080 |

A shape the canvas already has isn't in the list.

### Follow

What each movie clip keeps in the frame.

| Choice | What the frame follows |
| --- | --- |
| **Subject** | A face. Where there's no face, a person. Where there's neither, the region the eye goes to. |
| **Faces** | Faces only. |
| **People** | People only. |
| **Salient Region** | Only the region the eye goes to. |
| **Speaker** | Whoever is talking, for a wide shot with a microphone per person. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/). |
| **Center** | The middle of the picture, for the whole clip. Needs no analysis, so the summary is ready at once. |

These are the choices of [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), plus **Speaker**. The two commands share one remembered choice, saved when you choose **Make**. It starts on **Subject**. If you last chose **Speaker**, Follow Subject, which doesn't offer it, opens on **Subject**.

### Zoom

How tight the frame is, from 100 to 400 %, in whole numbers. 100 % is the smallest scale at which a picture covers the new canvas. Higher values frame closer.

**Zoom** starts at 100 % every time and isn't remembered. The summary catches up when you leave the field.

### Where Empty

What a followed clip shows while there's nothing to follow.

| Choice | What the frame shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Show Whole** | The whole picture on a blurred copy of itself. This is the default. |
| **Center** | The middle of the picture. |

It's off while **Follow** is **Center**. It's the same remembered choice as Follow Subject's.

### Make a copy

Ticked, the vertical version opens as a new untitled project and this project doesn't change. The copy is named after this project with the shape, such as "Interview (9:16)", "Interview (4:5)" or "Interview (1:1)". It carries the project's caches and analysis. Save it when you want to keep it.

Unticked, this project itself becomes the vertical version.

The box is ticked whenever the sheet opens, and your choice isn't remembered.

## Read the summary

Under the controls, the sheet says what **Make** will do, and it changes as you change a control. It opens with the new size, "Makes a 1080 × 1920 version.", and goes on with whichever of these apply:

| The summary says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Follows 3 clips." | Movie clips that follow what you chose. |
| "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced." | Screen recordings that follow the pointer. |
| "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip." | Wide shots framed on the speaker. |
| "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas." | Camera layout switches made again. |
| "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." | Clips with nothing to follow at any point. |
| "Keeps 4 clips as placed." | Clips moved and scaled to the new canvas, not framed. |
| "Re-fills 1 background." | Blurred copies and background plates resized to cover the new canvas. |
| "Removes 1 blurred copy the framing replaces." | Old blurred copies that are no longer needed. |
| "Re-sizes 1 graphic to the new canvas." | Graphics exactly the old canvas's size. |
| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | Older copies of a bundled template, in a copy only. |
| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | A new track at the back for the blurred copies. |
| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | A further track, for copies that overlap in time. |
| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | Actions on a clip eased again where the framing cuts. |
| "2 actions carry a framing move." | Actions that now carry a move of the framing as well. |
| "Re-lays 1 caption track for the new canvas." | Word captions paged again for the narrow frame. |

After those come single lines for what needs your attention:

- One line per camera layout switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
- One line per clip that isn't followed, or is only partly followed, with the reason: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." or "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found."
- One line per caption track that's kept as it was, and one per graphic module left as it is.

If the movies have already been analysed, the summary reads "Reading the analysis…" for a moment, and **Make** is dimmed until it's done.

If Frame Job can't make the new version, the summary says why and **Make** stays dimmed. That happens when a project is at its limit of 64 tracks, nests included, because Make Vertical needs a track for the blurred copies.

## When the movies need analysing

Following a subject needs to know where the faces, people and shot changes are. When the movies haven't been analysed yet, the summary says so: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."

**Make** then shows the Analyzing sheet while that runs on your Mac, and makes the version when it's done. **Stop** makes nothing: no project opens and this one doesn't change.

**Center** needs no analysis, and a recording that follows its pointer is never analysed. With **Speaker**, the sheet comes back after the analysis so you can [confirm who is on each microphone](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis).

If an analysis fails, Frame Job beeps, makes nothing and names the file at the foot of the inspector.

## Make another shape

What was found stays in this project's cache and is carried into the copy, so making another shape afterwards needs no analysis. Choose the command again on the landscape project and pick the next shape.

## Undo Make Vertical

The whole change is one undo step. In the copy, **Edit ▸ Undo Make Vertical** gives back the landscape edit. In place, it takes the command back on this project.

## Keep the picture sharp

A vertical canvas shows the middle of a landscape picture enlarged. A 1080p source framed on 1080 × 1920 is enlarged ×1.78, which can look soft on a phone, and a **Zoom** above 100 % enlarges it further. Shoot 4K for footage you mean to make vertical.

## Good to know

- Make Vertical works on the top-level timeline. A [nest](/editing/nests/) is treated as one clip, and what's inside it isn't reframed.
- If the project changes while the sheet is open or the analysis runs, nothing is made. Frame Job beeps and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while the Make Vertical Version sheet was open, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again." or "the project changed while Make Vertical was analyzing, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again."
- If the step wouldn't change the copy, the copy is closed and nothing is made: "Make Vertical did not apply to the copy, so nothing was made."

## With an agent

`make_vertical_version` makes the same version from a named shape. It differs from the sheet in a few ways:

- It can save the copy straight to a place you choose, and the assistant asks first when it does.
- It can leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again.
- It waits up to 60 s for an analysis. Past that nothing is made, and calling it again carries on.

See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

## Related

- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
- [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/)
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
- [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/)
- [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/)
- [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/)

---
title: What Make Vertical changes
description: Clip by clip, what Make Vertical Version does to movies, screen recordings, camera layouts, stills, graphics, captions and everything else.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) doesn't crop the timeline as one picture. It looks at each clip and treats it by what it is, so a talking head follows its subject while a title stays a title. This page says what happens to each kind of clip, and what the sheet's summary says about it.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…" tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']} />

## How a clip is judged

Every clip with a picture on the top-level timeline is judged on the old canvas. The first row that fits decides what happens to it.

| The clip | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| A [blurred copy](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) behind a clip | Removed, or re-filled to cover the new canvas |
| A [background plate](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) | Re-filled to cover the new canvas |
| A [graphic exactly the old canvas's size](#graphics) | Re-sized to the new canvas |
| A [camera or a screen in a camera layout](#camera-layouts) | Laid out again for the new canvas |
| A [screen recording with its cursor file](#screen-recordings) that fills the frame | Follows the pointer |
| A [movie](#full-frame-movies) that fills the frame | Follows its subject |
| A [still, picture or nest](#stills-pictures-and-nests) that fills the frame | Centred |
| [Word captions](#word-captions) | Paged again for the narrow frame |
| [Everything else](#everything-else) | Kept as placed |

A clip **fills the old frame** when its rectangle at its first frame covers the canvas on one side, to within a pixel at each edge, and on the other side is centred to within 2 % or covers that too. So the usual full-frame shot counts, and so does one punched in a little. A picture-in-picture doesn't.

A sound-only clip, a clip with its video turned off and an adjustment clip have no picture here, so nothing happens to them.

## Full-frame movies

A movie clip that fills the old frame follows what you chose in **Follow**, as [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) frames it. Its own moves and actions stay, inside the framing.

Where the frame shows the whole picture, a blurred copy of the clip goes behind it, so the canvas around it isn't empty. The copies go on a new **Backgrounds** track at the back, and copies that overlap in time go on further tracks behind it. The track is removed when no copy needs it.

The summary tells you how each one went:

| The clip | The summary says |
| --- | --- |
| Follows its subject | It's counted in "Follows 3 clips." |
| Has nothing to follow at any point | It's counted in "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." |
| Has nothing to follow for part of its length | It's still counted as followed, with "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found." |
| Moves by a motion of its own | "Clip 2 is followed, but moves by its own motion: …", with the motion's name, because that move isn't part of the framing. |

Some movies can't be followed and are kept as placed, each listed with the reason:

- A movie whose file is missing: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." With **Follow** on **Center** it's centred like any other clip instead.
- A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or one a matte cuts, because framing would move it out of the matte.
- A clip turned by its rotation or by an action, or one that spins in its motion, because framing works on an upright picture.

With **Follow** on **Speaker**, a wide shot beside its microphones cuts to whoever is talking, and every other movie follows its faces. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).

## Screen recordings

A screen recording with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) follows the pointer instead of a face, because a face on a screen isn't what the viewer is looking at.

- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when it strays from the middle of the frame, by more than 20 % of the frame's width or 12 % of its height.
- It arrives on each click. The move ends on the click's frame, so the click lands in view.
- It holds still while you type.
- Any zoom and pan of the clip's own, such as [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)'s, is replaced, since the tall frame is already a close-up. The summary says so: "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced."

**Where Empty** doesn't apply, because a pointer is always somewhere. **Center** centres the recording as any other movie.

When the cursor file can't be read, because it was moved or deleted, the recording is shown whole on a blurred copy and the summary says "its cursor file could not be read, so it is shown whole".

## Camera layouts

A screen recording and its camera in [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) keep their arrangement. This covers the layouts of **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** and the layout a recording landed in. Each switch is made again for the new canvas, at the same time, length and curve.

| On the old canvas | On the new canvas |
| --- | --- |
| A Corner | A Corner in the same corner |
| Camera Full | Camera Full |
| Side by Side, going to a tall canvas | Stacked, with the screen across the top and the camera below it, so the screen isn't squeezed into two-thirds of a narrow frame |
| Side by Side, going to a square | Side by Side |

The camera, the screen and the cut pieces of either are never followed and get no blurred copy. A zoom on the screen keeps showing the same part of the picture.

The summary counts them, "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas.", and lists each switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."

A circle or panel crop is re-centred on the middle of the crop it had. A crop that had room to move may sit nearer the middle of the camera picture than a switch made directly on the new canvas would.

### A layout changed by hand

If a camera was moved or resized by more than a pixel after its switch, it's no longer a layout Frame Job made. The camera and its screen are kept as placed, and the summary says "Clip 6 is not followed: its camera layout was edited by hand, so it is kept as placed."

## Stills, pictures and nests

A still or a picture that fills the frame is centred, and so is a [nest](/editing/nests/) that does. There's nothing inside them to follow. The summary lists each one: "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a still picture, so it is centred." or "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a nest, so it is centred."

What's inside a nest isn't reframed. A still, picture or nest that doesn't fill the frame is [kept as placed](#everything-else).

## Graphics

A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, such as a full-frame lower third or title card, is re-sized to the new canvas, so it lays itself out again on the narrow frame. Its position and the positions its actions move it to shrink and stretch with the two sides, and its scale stays as it was. Any other graphic is [kept as placed](#everything-else).

Older copies of the bundled templates in the project are updated in a copy, and listed when you apply the step in place: "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height is listed too, and never rewritten. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).

## Everything else

Titles, other graphics, shapes, a picture-in-picture and any clip that doesn't fill the frame are kept as placed. They're moved and scaled from the old canvas to the new one, as the Document tab does when a [canvas change](/projects/canvas-size/) rescales clips:

- A clip's horizontal position follows the change in width.
- Its vertical position follows the change in height.
- Its scale follows the smaller of the two changes, so something that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one.

From 1920 × 1080 to 1080 × 1920, a title's distance from the centre shrinks to 0.56 across and grows to 1.78 down, and the title itself shrinks to 0.56 of its size. The positions and scales its actions move to change the same way.

## Blurred copies and background plates

A blurred copy already behind a clip is removed when that clip is framed, because the framing makes a new one where it's needed. Otherwise it's re-filled to cover the new canvas. A copy counts as one when it's named **Blurred Background** and a clip of the same source, start and length sits in front of it.

A background plate from **Clip ▸ Add Background** is re-filled too. A plate is a rectangle shape the canvas's size, centred at scale 1, or an image or still named **Background** that fills the canvas. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).

## Word captions

Word captions are paged again for the narrow frame from the words their pages hold, every correction kept, as **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** does. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/). A track that was hidden or locked stays that way.

A caption track that can't be re-laid is kept as placed, and the summary names it: "Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings." That happens to [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/), and to a track when:

- it's a matte track
- a page has no word timings, or none of a page's words starts inside it
- a page is in a style Frame Job doesn't make, or its pages are in more than one style
- its pages wouldn't fit

## Related

- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
- [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/)
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
- [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/)
- [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/)
- [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/)

---
title: Follow the speaker in a vertical
description: Make a vertical version of a wide interview that cuts to whoever is talking, using a microphone per person.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A wide shot of two to four people doesn't fit a tall frame. Follow Speaker solves that: in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), it reads each person's microphone and cuts the frame to whoever is talking.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
  where="Follow ▸ Speaker in the sheet"
  tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']}
  needs="A microphone for each person, on its own track. Faces are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## What you need

- A wide shot: a full-frame movie clip with the people in it.
- A sound file for each person, from a recorder or a lavalier rather than a camera, each on its own track and recorded with the shot.
- Those sound files lined up with the shot. Use [**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**](/audio/synchronize-audio/) first.

## Follow the speaker

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** and set **Follow** to **Speaker**. The **Microphones** and **Faces** rows appear.

2. Under [**Microphones**](#microphones), tick the tracks that belong to the people in the shot, two to four.

3. Under [**Faces**](#faces), check that each row names that microphone's person. If the movies haven't been analysed yet the rows are empty for now.

4. Choose **Make**. If an analysis has to run first, [the sheet comes back](#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis) when it's done, so you can do step 3 and choose **Make** there.

</Steps>

The other controls work as they do in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/#the-controls).

## Microphones

A checkbox for each track holding a sound file, named by the track and listed front to back. A camera's track isn't offered, and neither is one whose sound is off. The first four are ticked.

Tick the ones that belong to the people in the shot.

When no full-frame movie plays beside two ticked microphones, the sheet says "No full-frame movie clip plays beside two of the ticked microphones, so nobody can be framed by who is talking." and **Make** stays off.

## Faces

One row per ticked microphone, with a pop-up of the faces Frame Job found in the longest shot it can frame this way. Faces are numbered left to right, with where each sits across the picture: **Face 1 (42 % across)**.

Ticking or unticking a microphone rebuilds the rows and offers the match again for the new set. Otherwise your own choice stands.

### The automatic match

Frame Job matches each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. When the match is clear the pop-ups are already set, and the note under them reads "Each microphone is matched to the face that talks with it; change one if it is wrong." Check that each row names that microphone's person.

A match is clear when every microphone agrees with its face to at least 0.2, on a scale where 1 is perfect agreement and 0 is none. A face is counted when it's in at least a quarter of the shot, and four faces at most are considered.

### Choose a face

When the faces don't show who is whose, because mouths are too still or too small to read, each pop-up says **Choose a face** and the note reads "The faces do not show clearly who is on each microphone: choose each microphone's face." Pick each microphone's face yourself.

If the shot shows fewer faces than you've ticked microphones, the pop-ups have no faces to offer. Untick the microphones of people who aren't in it.

## When Make is offered

**Make** is on when all of these are true:

- Two to four microphones are ticked.
- A shot plays beside two of them.
- Every ticked microphone has a face of its own. Two microphones can't share a face.

While an analysis is still to be made there are no faces to choose yet, so the last rule waits: **Make** is on with the first two, and pressing it runs the analysis.

When a microphone has only just been imported, it may still be being measured. The sheet says so in the words [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) uses, such as "The microphone on track 3 is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet. Try again in a moment." Choose the command again in a moment. A microphone with no speech under the shot stops **Make** in the same way, with "The microphone on track 3 has no speech between …". Untick it.

## The sheet comes back after analysis

The summary warns you first: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then asks you to confirm who is on each microphone, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."

When you choose **Make**, the Analyzing sheet runs. Then the sheet comes back on the same shape, **Follow**, **Zoom**, **Where Empty**, **Make a copy** and ticked microphones, this time with faces to confirm. Nothing is made until you choose **Make** there. **Stop** on the Analyzing sheet makes nothing.

## How the shot is cut

A shot is framed this way when it's a full-frame movie, its file is present, it has no cursor file, it isn't on a microphone track, and it overlaps sound on at least two ticked microphones. Frame Job doesn't count the people in it. The summary counts these shots: "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip."

Who talks when is read the way Switch by Speaker reads the microphones, with its default settings, so the two agree.

- Each change of speaker is a cut, not a move.
- Each framing holds at least 2 s, so a short reply doesn't cut away and back.
- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit. When they don't, the frame stays on the person already in it.
- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.

Every other movie clip follows its faces, and screen recordings and everything else are treated as usual. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).

## Shots that follow their faces instead

A shot that can't be framed by who is talking follows its faces instead, and the summary says why: "Clip 3 is followed, but it follows its faces, not who is talking, because …". The usual reasons are:

- It changes shot. Follow Speaker frames one wide shot, so split the clip first with **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**.
- It shows fewer faces than the microphones under it.
- Nobody talks inside it on those microphones.

## Good to know

- The faces you confirm come from the longest shot and apply to every shot by number, counting left to right. If people sit in a different order in another shot, that shot frames the wrong person.
- A shot uses only the ticked microphones that sound under it, so a microphone used elsewhere in the timeline doesn't count against it.
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) doesn't offer **Speaker**. Only Make Vertical Version and an agent do.

## With an agent

An agent makes the same version with `make_vertical_version`, naming two to four microphone clips, each standing for its track, and the faces if it wants to set them. Nobody confirms a match, so a shot whose faces don't show who is whose follows its faces, with the reason in the answer, unless the call names them. `reframe_clip` frames one clip on whoever is talking, on the canvas it's already on. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

## Related

- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>
